🇺🇦🇺🇸 Ukrainian participants in today's Kiev talks doubt the war will end before winter, the Financial Times reports, citing sources. According to the paper, Witkoff and Kushner brought few new ideas, mostly updated versions of previously published documents aimed at reviving interest in earlier proposals and narrowing the Russia-Ukraine gap. The central sticking point remains Donbass, with Moscow still insisting on a full Ukrainian withdrawal. The envoys reportedly discussed how to help Ukraine through a difficult winter as Russia intensifies strikes on infrastructure, while still assuring Zelensky's team they believe progress toward a settlement is achievable before then.

Zelensky thanked Witkoff and Kushner for the lack of strikes on Kiev during their visit: "You worked better today than the Patriot systems. Thank you, come more often." He acknowledged the war will likely continue into winter and said Ukraine is counting on a winter support package from the US, with expanded Patriot missile production and additional systems.

On Donbass, Zelensky pushed back on ceding the region for a peace deal: "The Donbass question isn't just about Donbass. Between us, I think it's the question of this whole war. We've gotten stronger on the battlefield in the east, where the enemy is active, where they've increased troop numbers, and where I believe Russia will run a mobilization specifically for this direction after their elections. A lot of geopolitical questions are really being decided there."

Axios reports, citing sources, that Witkoff and Kushner told Zelensky they want a breakthrough before winter and are working with Moscow and Kiev on an "updated" settlement proposal. Witkoff said a meeting between Russian, American, and Ukrainian representatives will be announced soon, calling his Moscow talks with Putin "constructive and substantive" — his eighth visit there, each time treated respectfully, he said. Kushner said the US is building a "peace package" and hopes to restart talks in a trilateral format with Russia, Ukraine, and the US.

Separately, Ukrainian outlet Glavcom published what it says are details of a "peace plan" Trump's envoys may have brought to Moscow and Kiev, and unconfirmed by any party: a full ceasefire, Ukrainian territorial concessions, AFU withdrawal from Donbass and part of Zaporozhye (with a possible UN contingent deployed there), a referendum and elections, constitutional changes, a renunciation of retaking Russian-controlled territory by force, non-bloc status for Ukraine with no NATO membership, limits on AFU troop numbers, language-policy provisions, and a full peace treaty signed by a new Ukrainian government, later formalized through the UN.
